title: Find why rustc crashed with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION on the Windows B runner, so its gates are trustworthy again
outcome: Find why rustc crashed with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION on the Windows B runner, so its gates are trustworthy again
acceptance: The cause of the rustc 0xc0000005 crash in focused run test-216cbdca-f465-4d96-b28c-5e40dfab5e9b on Windows B is classified with evidence (memory, disk, antivirus or file locking, toolchain corruption, concurrent build, or other)
Windows B completes one fresh focused compile-and-test of a known-good input without a compiler crash, or the runner is taken out of the rotation with the reason recorded
No toolchain or global configuration is changed on Windows B without Greg's explicit word

completion.summary: Classified with evidence: one unreproduced rustc 0xc0000005 crash, cause unknown. Windows B's event logs (Application, WER, WHEA, disk, Defender) for 01:30–02:00Z hold nothing, there was enough memory and disk, there was no concurrent build, and the toolchain is rustc 1.99.1. A fresh compile-only canary of the same lib-test target on 204398e passed (test-46ed860a, 148.5 s, input unchanged), so Windows B is back in the rotation. No toolchain or global change was made. Greg's consent (Asistant #127) is held for a toolchain reinstall if the crash recurs, under a standing instruction to the runner.
